summary: My slot was residual-stream topology. U-net skip connections clearly hurt (1.022087 vs 1.012347 baseline): the encoder outputs are already in the additive residual stream, so the skips only rescale it. Making the existing resid/x0 lambdas per-channel instead of per-layer scalars was a real but base-dependent win: -0.0024 on a0's 2**18 batch base (1.001286, cell best at the time), a wash on the MLP_RATIO=6 base (0.990240 with depth 10, my best run), and clearly negative on a1's depth-12 base (0.993828 vs 0.986500), partly because the vector multiply costs ~9GB of extra activations and hence steps. My last run tested FLOP-matched depth-for-MLP-width reallocation (depth 14 x MLP 3 vs depth 12 x MLP 4) and it lost by 0.0116, which together with a1's width result closes off FLOP re-allocation as a lever. Next I would stop adding capacity to b48980c (every stack on it has lost) and attack the optimization side that is still untouched at depth 12: the LR schedule shape (WARMDOWN_RATIO/FINAL_LR_FRAC), the embedding/unembedding LRs, and the logit softcap -- plus a3's non-threaded bisect dataloader, since the run is measurably CPU-side batch-building bound.
